name: program_options config-file (INI-style) parser
description:
parse_config_file<charT> reads an INI-style configuration file from an istream (or, via the filename overload, opens a file itself) and turns it into a sequence of basic_option<charT> values using the caller-supplied options_description as a whitelist of recognized long option names. This is the main untrusted-input entry point of Boost.ProgramOptions besides the command-line parser: the parser walks the stream line by line, strips comments/whitespace, recognizes "[section]" headers and "name = value" assignments, validates option names against the allowed set (exact match or "prefix*" wildcard), and throws typed exceptions (unknown_option, invalid_config_file_syntax) on malformed or unregistered input, making it security-relevant for any program that loads configuration from a file an attacker can influence.
- parse_config_file(istream, options_description, bool): target; constructs the set of allowed long names from options_description and drives boost::program_options::detail::basic_config_file_iterator/common_config_file_iterator over the stream, core = common_config_file_iterator::get()/add_option()/allowed_option().
- parse_config_file(const char* filename, options_description, bool): variant/source; opens an ifstream itself (exercises file-open/failure paths: reading_file exception) and then calls the istream overload, same core.
- options_description::add_options() / options_description_easy_init::operator(): configuration, builds the options_description fed to the target (names, whether an option is "name*" style, whether it is a required/positional-less value option) — these choices change which names are allowed_options vs allowed_prefixes and therefore which branch of allowed_option()/add_option() runs.
- parse_command_line / basic_command_line_parser::run(): variant producing the same basic_parsed_options<charT> result type from a different source (argv instead of a config stream), useful to combine sources the way the example programs do (command line overrides config file).
- store(basic_parsed_options<charT>&, variables_map&, bool): consumer; takes the parsed_options result of parse_config_file and performs the actual type conversion/validation of each value against the option's value_semantic (further exercising value parsing code triggered by attacker-controlled config content).
- notify(variables_map&): consumer; invokes the notifier callbacks/required-option checks after store(), reached via option values parsed from the config file.
Input space to fuzz: (1) the raw bytes of the config stream/content — comment lines starting with '#', blank lines, "[section]" headers (including malformed ones without closing ']'), "name = value" lines with varying whitespace, lines with no '=' and no '[' (triggers invalid_config_file_syntax), duplicate/unknown names (triggers unknown_option unless allow_unregistered is set); (2) the `allow_unregistered` boolean passed to parse_config_file, which is the most permissive setting (true lets unknown option names through with unregistered=true instead of throwing, exercising far more of the stream than the strict false mode which bails out on the first unrecognized name); (3) the options_description passed in — option names ending in '*' exercise the allowed_prefixes/wildcard-matching code path in add_option()/allowed_option(), plain names exercise exact-match lookup, and abbreviated (short-only) names make parse_config_file itself throw before any iteration.
This list is incomplete; what the project's own fuzzers and tests do with the target stays.
